clue.text: Digs for money in the US

definitions.meaning: digs is British slang for lodgings, a place where someone lives
the American coin worth twenty-five cents is a quarter, so these are coins

explanation.definitionFit: Lodgings are also called quarters, and a US twenty-five-cent coin is a quarter.

clue.text: Ships built in Britain for a New York borough

definitions.meaning: the great Cunard liners Queen Mary and Queen Elizabeth were built on the Clyde in Scotland
one of the five boroughs of New York City, alongside Brooklyn and the Bronx

explanation.definitionFit: The famous Cunard liners carried royal names, and one of New York City's five boroughs bears the same name.

clue.text: Fine sort of race in which to find me

indicators.note: the word me is to be found inside the rearranged letters
a sort of race is a reworked version of the word race, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle about some peculiar race in which the speaker turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' is a verb here, to impose a monetary penalty, not the adjective the surface suggests; AMERCE is an old legal word.
explanation.definitionFit: To amerce is an old legal verb meaning to punish with a monetary penalty.

clue.text: Small monkey with an old master

parts.note: the titi is a small South American monkey
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter of the old school pictured with a little monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian painter Titian is one of the great Renaissance painters, the sense of 'old master'.

clue.text: Introduces various price cuts

indicators.note: various suggests the letters take a different arrangement from the one printed

explanation.surface: A shop brings in several discounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowering what something costs is making a cut in its price.

clue.text: Vegetarian dishes for young Nazi storm-troopers?

parts.note: the SA (Sturmabteilung) were the Nazi brownshirt storm-troopers
young males are lads

explanation.surface: Asks whether meat-free food suits youthful brownshirts.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'SA lads', young members of the storm-troopers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowls of leaves and raw vegetables are meat-free meals.

clue.text: A talented artist rings a bell for her

indicators.note: rings means encircles, so the two letters for the artist wrap around the following words

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a distinguished artist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gifted painter sounds a bell to summon a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' puts A BELL inside RA; another A goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabella is a woman's given name, so a female pronoun stands for it.

clue.text: New Year gifts whose days are numbered

definitions.text: New Year gifts whose days are numbered

parts.words: New Year gifts whose days are numbered
parts.note: yearly reference books given at New Year list every date, so their days are literally numbered, and they go out of date after twelve months

explanation.definitionFit: Annual books of calendars and dates are traditional New Year presents that go stale when the year ends.

clue.text: Versatile danseuse of African nationality

indicators.note: versatile means able to turn to many forms, so the letters change shape

explanation.surface: A ballet dancer who can do many styles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Versatile' rearranges DANSEUSE, a female ballet dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Sudan, an African country, holds that nationality.

clue.text: Balanced sort of diet that comes rather late in the day

parts.note: balanced means level or even

indicators.note: a sort of diet is a variant of the word, so its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A healthy, balanced eating plan arrives in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the time when daylight is ending.

clue.text: Battered revolutionary with a couple of thousand tucked away

indicators.note: tucked away means stowed inside, so these letters go within the word for a revolutionary

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them

explanation.surface: A beaten-up radical who has hidden away a tidy sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battered' looks like an adjective about the revolutionary but is the definition, in its sense of struck hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rammed has been struck hard and repeatedly, like a battered door.

clue.text: Complete lack of opportunity for faultless batting?

definitions.meaning: an impossible prospect, nothing to hope for
in cricket a batter who gives no catches offers fielders nothing to take

explanation.definitionFit: A hopeless prospect is described this way, and in cricket an innings without a dropped catch gave fielders nothing.

clue.text: A standard author with no French following

parts.note: to author a piece is to pen it
non is French for no

explanation.surface: A writer of flags who refuses any French influence.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow flag, a kind of banner carried on a lance.

clue.text: Quest'oquella rendered in English?

parts.note: the Italian words questo o quella mean one item or another, and translating them gives an English phrase of choice

explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase translates word for word into an English expression offering a choice between two things.

clue.text: Mountain resorts in which VIPs predominate?

definitions.meaning: places at altitude, literally elevated spots
the idiom 'friends in ...' refers to people of influence

explanation.definitionFit: Resorts at altitude are literally elevated spots, and powerful people are said to occupy elevated positions.

clue.text: He'll make a song about artillery fire

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for making a song goes round the other piece

parts.note: to make a song is to sing
the letters of he'll without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone will make a fuss about the bombardment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a song about' is also an idiom meaning make a fuss over, which hides the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombarding with shells from big guns is the action of artillery.

clue.text: Free admission?

parts.note: entry with no restriction, as through an entrance left unlocked; also a policy of unrestricted access

explanation.definitionFit: An unrestricted access policy lets anyone in, like an entrance left unlocked.

clue.text: Antoine's inordinately privileged pupils

indicators.note: inordinately read as out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A boy named Antoine has unusually privileged schoolmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inordinately' rearranges ANTOINES; here the S of the possessive counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Boys at Eton College, an exclusive English boarding school, are seen as privileged pupils.

clue.text: The maximum length of a set square

definitions.text: The maximum length of a set square

parts.words: The maximum length of a set square
parts.note: a set square is a right-angled triangle used for drawing, and its longest edge is the side opposite the right angle

explanation.definitionFit: The side opposite the right angle in a right triangle is always its longest edge.

clue.text: French city packed with Marines for the opera

indicators.note: a city packed with something holds it inside

parts.note: Caen is a city in Normandy
RM is the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A French town full of soldiers for a night at the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Caen is in Normandy; the Royal Marines are Britain's naval infantry, abbreviated RM.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizet's opera about a Spanish gypsy bears this title.

clue.text: A Muslim who is lawfully employed

definitions.text: A Muslim who is lawfully employed

parts.words: A Muslim who is lawfully employed
parts.note: a Muslim cleric learned in sacred law works in the field of Islamic law, so his job is literally a lawful one

explanation.definitionFit: An Islamic cleric trained in religious law has law as his work.

clue.text: A container ship, possibly

definitions.meaning: a receptacle such as a jug or bowl
a boat is one example of a craft afloat

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a receptacle for liquid and a seagoing craft.

clue.text: Fish about in the inside of one's pocket, maybe

definitions.text: the inside of one's pocket, maybe

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fish goes round the following word

parts.note: ling is a fish of the cod family
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish about' reads as rummaging, but 'Fish' is the noun, a ling, a sea fish of the cod family.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabric sewn inside a pocket is its inner layer.

clue.text: Invaluable servant one would be lucky to find

definitions.meaning: a much-valued housekeeper or helper is affectionately called a gem

definitions.text: one would be lucky to find
definitions.meaning: buried riches are a lucky find

explanation.definitionFit: A prized helper is called this, as is hidden wealth that a lucky person might dig up.

clue.text: The places it links come under constant pressure

definitions.text: The places it links come under constant pressure

parts.words: The places it links come under constant pressure
parts.note: on a weather map a line joins places with equal atmospheric pressure

explanation.definitionFit: A meteorological line joining points of equal barometric pressure links places at the same pressure.

clue.text: But it isn't a terrible muddle in York!

definitions.text: But it isn't a terrible muddle in York!

parts.words: But it isn't a terrible muddle in York!
parts.note: the word means a terrible mess, but in York it is the name of a famous medieval street of old butchers' shops

explanation.walkthrough: The Shambles is a narrow, picturesque medieval street in the English city of York.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday sense is a chaotic mess, while York's well-known old street bears this name.

clue.text: Gaudy hags cavorting round Rhode Island

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the state abbreviation
cavorting means prancing about, so the letters jump into a new order

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state

explanation.surface: Flashy old women dancing around an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' rearranges the letters of hags into GASH before the state's abbreviation is placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish means showy and loud in colour, just like gaudy.

clue.text: French-speaking writer from Shetland

indicators.note: from here signals that the writer's name is made out of the letters of the next word, rearranged

explanation.surface: A Francophone author who comes from the Scottish isles.
explanation.definitionFit: Stendhal, author of The Red and the Black, was a French novelist.
